title: Intelligent Data Capture & Schedule-Linking Layer for Infrastructure Project Management: Real-Time Actual Progress Tracking (Planning-to-Execution Bridge)
description:
• Background Infrastructure project schedules cascade from macro milestones (L1) down to micro, executable activities (L5/L6),spanning multiple engineering disciplines - civil, piping, static/rotating equipment, electrical, instrumentation, HSE- each executing and reporting in parallel. While the baseline plan is well-structured (Primavera/MS Project), actual execution data flows back through daily progress reports, site diaries, discipline-wise spreadsheets, and verbal supervisor updates, each in its own format and cadence, largely disconnected from the L5/L6 activity IDs in the plan.
• Problem Description There is no reliable, low-friction mechanism to capture actual start/end times of L5/L6 activities across disciplines and auto-link them back to the plan. Input quality varies with manpower skill, reporting discipline, and format.Field execution is often more granular than the planned WBS, and different disciplines describe the same physical progress differently (e.g., 'spool erected' vs. the plan's 'Erect Line 24?-XX').Consequently:
? Actual progress data is fragmented, delayed, and inconsistently structured across disciplines and contractors.
? Manual reconciliation with the baseline schedule is slow, error-prone, and often lags the schedule update cycle by days or weeks.
? Downstream performance analytics, delay/ risk analysis, and forecasting inherit this poor-quality, late data- undermining the AI performance-monitoring stack that depends on it.
? Once a project closes, the hard-won knowledge of what actually happened - real durations, real bottlenecks,real deviations from plan - is rarely captured in a structured, queryable form, so it is lost rather than feeding future project planning.
• Expected Outcome/Solution ? Ingest heterogeneous discipline-wise inputs - free-text daily reports, spreadsheets, scanned diaries,Primavera/MS Project exports - and extract activity-level actual start/end events.
? Offer an LLM-based conversational or voice interface ('time agent') for site supervisors across disciplines to log activity start/end with minimal friction, replacing rigid manual forms while still producing structured output.
? Fuzzy-match and link extracted discipline-specific activity descriptions to the correct L5/L6 plan node,handling terminology differences and granularity mismatches, and flag unmatched/new activities for planner review rather than silently dropping them.
? Auto-update actual start/end dates in the schedule/PMIS in near real time, with a confidence score and audit trail per entry.
? Produce a clean, structured, discipline-tagged actual-progress dataset that serves two purposes: (a) live input for performance analytics, delay/risk pattern discovery, and forecasting, and (b) a foundation for institutional memory building - a growing, queryable repository of real project execution patterns (actual durations, recurring delay causes, discipline-wise productivity) that future projects can learn from, instead of that knowledge staying locked in individual supervisors' experience or scattered paper records.
A working prototype demonstrating ingestion of 2–3 varied input formats (e.g., a free-text daily report and a discipline spreadsheet), extraction, and schedule-linking logic would be ideal; full production-grade OCR/ASR is not required.
• Relevant Data Availability Anonymized/ sample daily progress report formats, sample L5/L6 schedule extracts, and illustrative discipline-wise (civil/ piping/ electrical) site-diary or spreadsheet templates can be shared under NDA with Institute/ Authorised person. Live project data will not be shared; teams should work with synthetic/sample data of similar structure.
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on ai, llm applied to a smart automation problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Automation. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on real-time, infrastructure. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 19/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Intelligent Data Capture & Schedule-Linking Layer for Infrastructure Project Management

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that automatically links messy, inconsistent field progress reports, spreadsheets, site diaries, different descriptions for the same physical work, back to the exact planned activity in a formal project schedule, closing the gap between what's planned and what's actually happening on site.
overview.why_it_matters: Right now, actual field progress data is fragmented and disconnected from the formal plan, making reconciliation slow and manual. Automating that link gives real-time visibility into true project status.
pain_points: Actual execution data is fragmented across disciplines, formats, and reporting cadences.
Field progress reporting is more granular than the planned WBS, and different disciplines describe the same work differently.
No reliable, low-friction mechanism auto-links field-reported progress back to specific planned activity IDs.
overview.background: Infrastructure project schedules are well-structured in planning tools, but actual field execution data flows back through inconsistent formats and terminology, disconnected from the plan's activity structure, requiring slow manual reconciliation.
overview.whats_being_asked: An intelligent data-capture layer that captures actual start/end times of granular field activities across disciplines and auto-links them back to the formal L5/L6 schedule activity IDs.
expected_solution: Low-friction field data capture across disciplines (civil, piping, electrical, etc.).
NLP-based matching of field-reported activities (varied terminology) to formal schedule activity IDs.
Automated reconciliation of actual progress against the baseline plan.
Handling of granularity mismatches between field reporting and planned WBS.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: High. Genuine NLP-based matching between inconsistent, jargon-heavy field terminology ('spool erected') and formal schedule nomenclature ('Erect Line 24-XX') is a real, hard entity-resolution challenge specific to this domain.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate-high. Achievable using semantic-matching NLP techniques applied thoughtfully; the harder part is handling genuine terminology and granularity mismatches across multiple engineering disciplines.

competitive_landscape.note: Highly specialized industrial project-management PS, requires genuine understanding of both NLP matching and multi-discipline construction/engineering terminology.

innovation.note: Genuine terminology-matching challenge across field jargon and formal schedule nomenclature is a real, specific, hard NLP problem.

invention.note: Semantic matching techniques are established; real effort in handling genuine discipline-specific terminology variation and granularity mismatches.

technical_feasibility.note: No hard external data dependency, this can be demonstrated convincingly with realistic constructed sample data across multiple disciplines.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly reduces manual reconciliation effort and improves real-time project visibility, genuine operational efficiency value.

architecture.note: A semantic-matching pipeline connecting field capture to schedule activities, well-understood pattern applied to a specific, hard matching problem.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, genuinely achievable with realistic synthetic data. The real differentiator is handling genuine terminology mismatch well ('spool erected' matching 'Erect Line 24-XX'), invest real effort in constructing tricky, realistic matching test cases across multiple disciplines.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very well-specified, concrete example of the actual matching challenge (the PS gives a direct example: 'spool erected' vs. 'Erect Line 24-XX'), giving clear guidance on what genuine success looks like.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Testing your matching system only against easy, obviously-similar terminology pairs would understate the real challenge, which is genuinely mismatched terminology across different disciplines' natural language habits.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Construct genuinely tricky, realistic terminology-mismatch test cases across multiple disciplines (civil, piping, electrical each describing progress differently) rather than easy, obviously-similar matching pairs.

idea_0_4: Research real construction/engineering field-reporting terminology across at least 2-3 disciplines to ground your synthetic dataset.
Construct a realistic synthetic schedule (formal L5/L6 activities) plus realistic field-report entries with genuine terminology mismatches.
Split: one person on the semantic-matching model, one on the data-capture interface.
prototype_4_22: Build your semantic-matching model connecting field-reported entries to formal schedule activity IDs.
Test against your constructed tricky terminology-mismatch cases specifically.
Start the low-friction field data-capture interface.
integration_22_30: Connect capture and matching into one coherent pipeline, showing auto-linked progress against the baseline schedule.
Refine matching based on your discrimination test results.
Build a reconciliation dashboard showing actual versus planned progress.
polish_30_36: Polish the dashboard for genuine project-management usability.
Rehearse presenting your matching system correctly handling a genuinely tricky terminology-mismatch case live.
Prepare to discuss your matching precision/recall against your constructed test cases.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your system correctly matching the PS's own example, a field report saying 'spool erected' correctly linking to the formal schedule activity 'Erect Line 24-XX', live, that direct demonstration of solving the PS's own stated example is concrete, credible proof.

strengths: Very well-specified example of the actual matching challenge gives clear success criteria.
No hard external data dependency, fully demonstrable with realistic constructed data.
weaknesses: Genuine terminology mismatch across multiple disciplines is a hard matching problem, easy to underbuild with only easy test cases.
Real-world deployment would need integration with actual field-reporting workflows and existing planning tools.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: NLP-weighted, with real domain research into multi-discipline field terminology.
team_fit.approach: Research real field-reporting terminology across multiple disciplines before constructing test cases, generic random variation won't reflect the actual matching challenge.

ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Constructing genuinely realistic, discipline-specific terminology-mismatch test cases, and correctly interpreting whether matches make real construction-domain sense.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: A matching model tested only against easy, obviously-similar examples would prove little about real-world performance against genuinely messy, discipline-varied field terminology.

data_resource_availability.status: No real Oil India project data accessible; a well-researched synthetic dataset reflecting real construction/engineering terminology conventions is the practical and appropriate path.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not applicable, synthetic construction is the intended approach here.

judge_qna.question: How does your matching handle the exact 'spool erected' versus 'Erect Line 24-XX' example given in the problem statement?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Demonstrate this specific case live, walking through how your semantic matching bridges the terminology gap.
judge_qna.follow_up: What other terminology mismatch patterns did you test across different disciplines?

judge_qna.question: How does your system handle field reporting that's more granular than the planned WBS, as the PS describes?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe your approach to granularity mismatches, whether aggregating multiple field reports to one schedule activity or flagging genuine granularity gaps for human review.
judge_qna.follow_up: What happens when field-level granularity reveals the plan itself was insufficiently detailed?
